questions.question: A student measures the length of a rod as 37.5 ± 0.1 cm. The uncertainty in this measurement is primarily due to:

options.B: The skill level of the experimenter
options.C: The least count of the measuring instrument

questions.explanation: The uncertainty in a single measurement of a physical quantity is usually taken as the least count of the instrument used. This defines the limit of resolution of the measurement.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of quantities have the same dimensions?
questions.explanation: Work, Energy, and Torque all have the same dimensions because each depends on force multiplied by distance.

questions.explanation: Both sides of the equation have identical dimensions, so the equation is dimensionally correct.

questions.question: The time period of a simple pendulum is proportional to √(l/g). If the length l is doubled and g is halved, the time period becomes:
questions.explanation: If the pendulum length becomes four times larger, the time period doubles because the time period is proportional to the square root of length.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dimensionless variable?
questions.explanation: Plane angle is dimensionless because it is the ratio of arc length to radius.

questions.question: The number of heartbeats in a 60-year human lifetime is approximately:
questions.explanation: The human heart beats approximately 1.8 × 10⁹ times in 60 years, giving an order of magnitude of 10⁹.

questions.question: Absolute uncertainty in a measurement is equal to:

options.D: Range of values ÷ Number of readings

questions.explanation: In a single measurement, the absolute uncertainty equals the least count of the instrument.

questions.question: If z = x − y, the absolute uncertainty Δz is:
questions.explanation: In addition and subtraction, absolute uncertainties are added together.

questions.question: The dimension of electric charge in SI base units is:
questions.explanation: Charge equals current multiplied by time, so its dimensions are based on current and time.
